---
title: "Is it a good assumption that there are no pitch dynamics, at this level of fidelity?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

Longitudinal modal timescales at the best-glide condition, then the same launch
released from 2 m flown twice on one aero table — once with angle of attack
pinned at trim, once with pitch attitude and pitch rate as free states.

Pitch inertia comes from the mass build-up below, which distributes the assumed
12 g all-up mass. The CG is assumed to sit at the model's moment reference. The
stabilizer incidence that would trim the aircraft is not modelled, so it is
stood in for by a constant pitching-moment offset. The aero table is clamped at
16°, above which the section data would be extrapolated, so excursions beyond
that angle are held at the 16° coefficients.

**Answer.** For a release at trim speed, yes — the two models agree to within
0.1%, and angle of attack never leaves 5.7°–6.5°. For a launch above trim speed,
no. The short period is not the reason: it is fast and well damped. The reason
is kinematic — angle of attack is the difference between pitch attitude and
flight path angle, and over the top of a zoom the flight path drops faster than
the airframe pitches down, driving angle of attack past stall. A fixed angle of
attack cannot represent that excursion at any level of pitch damping.

```{python}
import numpy as onp
from scipy.interpolate import RegularGridInterpolator

g, rho = 9.81, 1.225
m  = 0.012            # kg, ASSUMED all-up mass
h0 = 2.0              # m, ASSUMED release height
W  = m * g
V_trim, a_trim = 4.41, 6.0   # best-glide condition

# Pitch inertia. 5.8 g of this is the flying surfaces; the rest is the boom and
# the nose ballast that puts the CG at the model's moment reference.
x_cg = x_qc_w
parts = [  # (mass [kg], x [m], own inertia [kg m^2])
    (S_w * t_foam * rho_foam, 0.5 * c_w, 0.0),
    (S_h * t_foam * rho_foam, x_qc_t, 0.0),
    (S_v * t_foam * rho_foam, x_qc_t, 0.0),
    (0.0042, -0.030, 0.0),                      # nose ballast
    (0.0020, 0.100, 0.0020 * 0.20 ** 2 / 12),   # 0.2 m boom, uniform
]
Iyy = sum(mi * (xi - x_cg) ** 2 + Ii for mi, xi, Ii in parts)
print(f"mass {sum(p[0] for p in parts)*1000:.1f} g, Iyy = {Iyy:.3e} kg m^2, "
      f"radius of gyration = {(Iyy/sum(p[0] for p in parts))**0.5*1000:.0f} mm")
```

```{python}
op = asb.OperatingPoint(velocity=V_trim, alpha=a_trim)
d = asb.AeroBuildup(airplane=bfg, op_point=op).run_with_stability_derivatives()
CLa, Cma, Cmq = float(d["CLa"][0]), float(d["Cma"][0]), float(d["Cmq"][0])
LD = float(d["CL"][0]) / float(d["CD"][0])
print(f"CLa = {CLa:.2f}/rad, Cma = {Cma:.3f}/rad, Cmq = {Cmq:.2f}, "
      f"x_np = {float(d['x_np'][0]):.4f} m "
      f"(static margin {(float(d['x_np'][0]) - x_cg)/c_w*100:.0f}% MAC)")

# Short period from the two-state [alpha, q] approximation; phugoid from the
# standard Lanchester result, whose damping is set entirely by L/D.
q_dyn = 0.5 * rho * V_trim ** 2
Za = q_dyn * S_w * CLa / (m * V_trim)                       # 1/s
Ma = q_dyn * S_w * c_w * Cma / Iyy                          # 1/s^2
Mq = q_dyn * S_w * c_w ** 2 * Cmq / (2 * V_trim * Iyy)      # 1/s

w_sp = (-Ma - Za * Mq) ** 0.5
z_sp = (Za - Mq) / (2 * w_sp)
w_ph = g * 2 ** 0.5 / V_trim
z_ph = 1 / (2 ** 0.5 * LD)

print(f"short period: T = {2*onp.pi/w_sp:5.2f} s, zeta = {z_sp:.2f}, "
      f"settles (2%) in {4/(z_sp*w_sp):.2f} s")
print(f"phugoid:      T = {2*onp.pi/w_ph:5.2f} s, zeta = {z_ph:.2f}, "
      f"settles (2%) in {4/(z_ph*w_ph):.1f} s")
print(f"T_phugoid / T_short_period = {w_sp/w_ph:.1f}")
```

```{python}
# One aero table over (alpha, V), so both trajectory models see identical
# aerodynamics and the only difference between them is the pitch freedom.
al_grid = onp.linspace(-6, 16, 45)
V_grid = onp.array([2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.5, 8.0, 10.0, 12.5, 15.0, 18.0])

CL_t = onp.zeros((len(al_grid), len(V_grid)))
CD_t, Cm_t = onp.zeros_like(CL_t), onp.zeros_like(CL_t)
for j, V in enumerate(V_grid):
    p = polars(al_grid, V=float(V))
    CL_t[:, j], CD_t[:, j], Cm_t[:, j] = p["CL"], p["CD"], p["Cm"]

Cm_offset = -float(polars(np.array([a_trim]), V=V_trim)["Cm"][0])

kw = dict(bounds_error=False, fill_value=None)
fCL = RegularGridInterpolator((al_grid, V_grid), CL_t, **kw)
fCD = RegularGridInterpolator((al_grid, V_grid), CD_t, **kw)
fCm = RegularGridInterpolator((al_grid, V_grid), Cm_t + Cm_offset, **kw)


def coeffs(al_deg, V):
    """Clamped at the table edges -- see the note on 16° above."""
    pt = onp.array([[onp.clip(al_deg, -6, 16), onp.clip(V, 2.0, 18.0)]])
    return float(fCL(pt)[0]), float(fCD(pt)[0]), float(fCm(pt)[0])


def fly(V0, pitching, dt=0.0005):
    """
    Level release at V0 from h0.

    pitching=False pins alpha at trim, so only V and the flight path angle are
    states. pitching=True adds pitch attitude and pitch rate, making alpha the
    difference between attitude and flight path.
    """
    x, z, V, gam = 0.0, h0, V0, 0.0
    th, qr = onp.radians(a_trim), 0.0
    xs, zs, als = [x], [z], [a_trim]
    t = 0.0
    while z > 0 and t < 60:
        al = onp.degrees(th - gam) if pitching else a_trim
        CL, CD, Cm = coeffs(al, V)
        q_ = 0.5 * rho * V ** 2
        L, D = q_ * S_w * CL, q_ * S_w * CD
        if pitching:
            M = q_ * S_w * c_w * (Cm + Cmq * qr * c_w / (2 * max(V, 0.5)))
            qr += (M / Iyy) * dt
            th += qr * dt
        V = max(V + ((-D - W * onp.sin(gam)) / m) * dt, 0.5)
        gam += ((L - W * onp.cos(gam)) / (m * V)) * dt
        x += V * onp.cos(gam) * dt
        z += V * onp.sin(gam) * dt
        xs.append(x); zs.append(z); als.append(al); t += dt
    return onp.array(xs), onp.array(zs), onp.array(als)


launch_speeds = [4.4, 6.0, 8.0, 10.0, 12.0]
runs = {V0: (fly(V0, False), fly(V0, True)) for V0 in launch_speeds}

print(" V0 [m/s]   fixed-alpha [m]   free-pitch [m]    diff   alpha range [deg]")
for V0, ((xf, zf, af), (xp, zp, ap)) in runs.items():
    print(f"{V0:8.1f} {xf[-1]:17.1f} {xp[-1]:16.1f} {100*(xp[-1]-xf[-1])/xf[-1]:+7.0f}%"
          f"   {ap.min():6.1f} to {ap.max():6.1f}")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-pitch-freedom
#| fig-cap: "Above: flight path with angle of attack pinned at trim (dashed) and with pitch free (solid). Below: angle of attack of the free-pitch runs, with the trim value dotted."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 5), sharex=True)

for V0, colour in zip([4.4, 8.0, 12.0], ["C0", "C2", "C3"]):
    (xf, zf, af), (xp, zp, ap) = runs[V0]
    ax[0].plot(xf, zf, colour, ls="--", alpha=0.6)
    ax[0].plot(xp, zp, colour, label=f"{V0} m/s")
    ax[1].plot(xp, ap, colour, label=f"{V0} m/s")

ax[0].plot([], [], "k--", alpha=0.6, label="alpha pinned at trim")
ax[0].plot([], [], "k-", label="pitch free")
ax[0].set_ylabel("height [m]")
ax[0].legend(fontsize=7)
ax[0].grid(alpha=0.3)

ax[1].axhline(a_trim, color="k", lw=0.8, ls=":")
ax[1].set_xlabel("range [m]")
ax[1].set_ylabel(r"$\alpha$ [deg]")
ax[1].legend(fontsize=7)
ax[1].grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
